arth-01-c1.text: Emma Groeneveld (2016). Lascaux Cave. World History Encyclopedia.
arth-01-c1.quote: On 12 September 1940 CE four boys examined the foxhole down which their dog had fallen on the hill of Lascaux.
arth-01-c1.claim: On 12 September 1940 four boys examined the foxhole down which their dog had fallen on the hill of Lascaux, in the Dordogne region of south-western France.

arth-01-c1.text: Emma Groeneveld (2016). Lascaux Cave. World History Encyclopedia.
arth-01-c1.quote: The closest known source is some 250 kilometres (155 miles) away, in the central Pyrenees, which might point to a trade or supply route.
arth-01-c1.claim: Here is a puzzle: the nearest known source of Lascaux's particular manganese oxides is some 250 kilometres away, in the central Pyrenees.

arth-01-c1.text: Emma Groeneveld (2017). Chauvet Cave. World History Encyclopedia.
arth-01-c1.quote: the main scene shows a pride of 16 lions (indicated mostly by just their heads) chasing a group of seven bison.
arth-01-c1.claim: In the Panel of the Lions, a pride of 16 lions chases seven bison across a wall that was scraped clean first, with shading smudged in by hand

arth-01-c2.text: University of Southampton (2018). Earliest cave paintings were made by Neanderthals. University of Southampton News.
arth-01-c2.quote: shows that paintings in three caves in Spain were created more than 64,000 years ago – 20,000 years before modern humans arrived in Europe.
arth-01-c2.claim: That is about 20,000 years before modern humans reached Europe, so the team argued the painters must have been Neanderthals, Europe's only humans at the time.

arth-01-c2.text: Archaeology Magazine (2019). Dating Questions Spark Neanderthal Cave Art Debate. Archaeology (Archaeological Institute of America).
arth-01-c2.quote: This would mean the Spanish cave art could be tens of thousands of years more recent, and well within the timeframe of modern humans.
arth-01-c2.claim: the paintings could be tens of thousands of years younger, well within the time of modern humans

arth-01-c2.text: Africa Pitarch Martí, João Zilhão, Francesco d'Errico et al (2021). The symbolic role of the underground world among Middle Paleolithic Neanderthals. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
arth-01-c2.quote: we confirm that the paintings on a large speleothem from one of these sites, Cueva de Ardales, were human made, and we show that the pigments do not come from the outcrops of colorant material known inside the cave
arth-01-c2.claim: they confirmed the marks were human-made, and they showed the pigment did not come from the iron-rich deposits known inside the cave

arth-01-c3.text: Gerhard W. Weber, Alexander Lukeneder, Mathias Harzhauser et al (2022). The microstructure and the origin of the Venus from Willendorf. Scientific Reports.
arth-01-c3.quote: is exactly 110 mm in height and represents a symbolized adult and faceless female with exaggerated genitalia, pronounced haunches, a protruding belly, heavy breasts, and a sophisticated headdress or hairdo
arth-01-c3.claim: She is exactly 110 millimetres tall: faceless, with heavy breasts, a protruding belly and a carefully worked headdress or hairstyle covering her head.

arth-01-c3.text: Gerhard W. Weber, Alexander Lukeneder, Mathias Harzhauser et al (2022). The microstructure and the origin of the Venus from Willendorf. Scientific Reports.
arth-01-c3.quote: Sampling numerous oolite occurrences ranging ~ 2500 km from France to the Ukraine, we found a strikingly close match for grain size distribution near Lake Garda in the Southern Alps (Italy).
arth-01-c3.claim: Comparing her grains with oolite samples from France to Ukraine, they found the closest match at Sega di Ala, near Lake Garda in northern Italy, with a site in eastern Ukraine as a less likely second.

arth-01-c3.text: Jessica Liew (2017). Venus Figurine. World History Encyclopedia.
arth-01-c3.quote: “When paleoanthropologists refer to figurines as Venuses, [they] usually do so with air quotes” (von Petzinger, 95), because Venus figurines pre-date myths about the goddess Venus by thousands of years.
arth-01-c3.claim: these figures are thousands of years older than any myth of the Roman goddess Venus, and archaeologists usually say the word with air quotes

arth-02-c2.claim: Sanctuaries employed cleaners and polishers to keep statues a shiny reddish-brass colour.
